Classic Independence Day Berry Pie

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 55 min

This vibrant Berry Pie, bursting with the flavors of summer, is a quintessential dessert for Independence Day celebrations. Its red, white, and blue hues from mixed berries make it a festive and delicious centerpiece for any Fourth of July picnic or barbecue, symbolizing the spirit of the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 recipe (2 discs) for a double 9-inch pie crust, chilled (store-bought or homemade)
  • 3 cups (450 g) fresh blueberries
  • 2 cups (250 g) fresh raspberries
  • 1 cup (150 g) fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) cornstarch
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) fresh lemon juice
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 g) salt
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
  • 1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon (15 mL) water (for egg wash, optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. In a large bowl, gently combine the blueberries, raspberries, and sliced strawberries.
  3. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the granulated sugar, cornstarch, and salt.
  4. Pour the sugar mixture over the berries and add the lemon juice. Gently toss until the berries are evenly coated.
  5. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of pie crust into a 12-inch (30 cm) circle. Carefully transfer it to a 9-inch (23 cm) pie plate, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides.
  6. Pour the berry filling into the pie crust-lined plate. Dot the top of the filling with the small pieces of butter.
  7. Roll out the second disc of pie crust. You can either place it whole over the filling, cutting a few slits for steam to escape, or cut it into strips to create a lattice top.
  8. Place the top crust over the filling (or arrange lattice strips). Trim any excess dough, leaving about a 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) overhang. Fold the overhang under and crimp the edges decoratively with your fingers or a fork to seal.
  9. If desired, brush the top crust with the egg wash for a golden, shiny finish.
  10. Place the pie on a baking sheet to catch any potential drips. Bake for 20 minutes at 400°F (200°C).
  11. Reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for another 35-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly and thickened. If the crust starts to brown too quickly, loosely tent the pie with aluminum foil.
  12. Remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack for at least 3-4 hours before slicing and serving. This allows the filling to set properly.

Tips

  • For a firmer filling, ensure your berries are not overly wet. If using frozen berries, thaw them completely and drain any excess liquid before mixing with sugar and cornstarch.
  • To prevent a soggy bottom crust, you can sprinkle a thin layer of fine breadcrumbs or crushed cornflakes on the bottom crust before adding the filling.
  • Serve your Berry Pie slightly warm or at room temperature, perhaps with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream for an extra festive treat.
